queue_items.claim: The cluster's sole cohesion evidence is presented as an identical repeated word with a single pointed splice covering all four verses, and that is byte-false at the fourth verse: the anaphora is identical only once accents are stripped, and no tier is named.
queue_items.grounds: Spliced from source bytes the four openers are דּ֭וֹר (oshb:Prov.30.11), דּ֭וֹר (oshb:Prov.30.12), דּ֭וֹר (oshb:Prov.30.13) and דּ֤וֹר (oshb:Prov.30.14); the first three are codepoint-equal to each other but the fourth is not - it carries a different cantillation accent (U+05A4 in place of U+05AD) - so the set is byte-identical at three sites, not four. At accent-stripped tier and at skeleton tier all four are identical, and a skeleton sweep of the generation-word returns 5 verses book-wide (27:24 plus these four), so the anaphoric chain itself is byte-grounded and the 4-of-4 digit is true at the tier that supports it. The defect is that boundary_rationale asserts 'the identical word' with one pointed splice cited to the whole four-verse range, and observed_substrate_signals repeats that same pointed form as 'repeated at' all four refs, naming no tier - the campaign's tier discipline permits an identity claim only per collate truth with the tier stated. Because a range-scoped collation resolves against the concatenated window, the citation passes the machine binding while the claim it makes is still false at the fourth site.
queue_items.proposed_change: Field repair, span unchanged at Prov.30.11-Prov.30.14: state the tier (identical at accent-stripped and skeleton tier, four of four verse-initial), and splice the fourth verse's own opener separately with its own inline ref instead of covering all four with one pointed form.

queue_items.claim: A book-wide rare verb straddles the row's front seam as an adjacent pair and is undisclosed: the skeleton form sweeps to exactly two verses in the entire book, and they are the two verses on either side of this seam - while the preceding row asserts without qualification that its verse shares no catchword with this run.
queue_items.grounds: The row's refs cover its own span, the mark at its closing verse, a homograph-disambiguation site and the following verse, but nothing at the front edge. Weighing both sides from source bytes: the preceding row's closing verse opens אַל תַּלְשֵׁ֣ן עֶ֭בֶד (oshb:Prov.30.10) and carries יְקַלֶּלְךָ֥ (oshb:Prov.30.10), while the row's opening verse carries יְקַלֵּ֑ל (oshb:Prov.30.11) - the same curse-verb, and a skeleton sweep of that prefixed form returns exactly 2 verses book-wide, oshb:Prov.30.10 and oshb:Prov.30.11, with the wider three-letter root returning 5 (20:20, 26:2, 27:14, 30:10, 30:11). Count-object discipline matters here and cuts both ways: at the ruled shared-content-token object the two forms are different tokens and the seam is clean, which is what makes the preceding row's flat 'no catchword' sentence defensible - but that sentence names no object, and at root or substring level the link is not only real but book-wide unique to this adjacent pair, so it is owed a disclosure at whichever edge claims it away. What decides the seam is the anaphoric opener chain, absent from oshb:Prov.30.10, which opens on a prohibition instead; the back seam is separately sound, the row's closing verse sharing no skeleton content token with the following row's opening לַֽעֲלוּקָ֨ה שְׁתֵּ֥י בָנוֹת֮ (oshb:Prov.30.15) and the WLC petuchah after the closing verse corroborating it as single-witness tier-3, correctly disclosed and inventory-validated. No respan follows.
queue_items.proposed_change: Field repair, span unchanged at Prov.30.11-Prov.30.14: add oshb:Prov.30.10 to boundary_evidence_refs and one sentence naming the swept object and the digit (prefixed curse-form, 2 verses book-wide, both at this seam) and disposing of it against the anaphoric chain. The preceding row's unqualified no-catchword sentence needs the same object named; that is recorded for adjudication and is not applied here.

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: Four consecutive verses open with the identical word דּ֭וֹר (oshb:Prov.30.11-Prov.30.14, "a generation who..."), an anaphoric chain naming a byte-grounded construction-run (4 of 4 verses share the same opening token, sweep: 4 of 4) rather than a shared theme alone. The run closes on the sword-sense homograph חֲרָב֣וֹת שִׁנָּיו֮ (oshb:Prov.30.14, "teeth are like swords"), describing teeth rather than a foodstuff or a place-name -- distinct from the dry-morsel sense of the same root argued elsewhere at web:Prov.17.1. The petuchah at oshb:Prov.30.14 (single-witness, disclosed) corroborates the run's close before the leech saying at web:Prov.30.15.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Four separate single-verse rows were considered, since each "generation" line is grammatically complete on its own, but the identical opening word repeated across all four lines is exactly the kind of construction-run cohesion the collection's granularity rule treats as cluster-grade evidence, not a merely thematic grouping.
observed_substrate_signals: anaphoric opener דּ֭וֹר repeated at oshb:Prov.30.11, oshb:Prov.30.12, oshb:Prov.30.13, oshb:Prov.30.14
sword-sense token חֲרָב֣וֹת at oshb:Prov.30.14 (not the web:Prov.17.1 dry-morsel homograph)
petuchah closing the run at oshb:Prov.30.14 (single-witness)
shipped_row.device_notes: Parallelism class synthetic/descriptive: the four lines (4 of 4) complete parallel portraits of arrogance or filial contempt, rather than contrasting two clauses; the anaphora itself, not the shared theme, is the cluster's cohesion evidence. The proverb_cluster call here departs from C6's numerical-saying default on the anaphoric opening-word chain argued above (4 of 4), not by exception.

prev_row.boundary_rationale: A self-contained admonition about household loyalty, אַל תַּלְשֵׁ֣ן עֶ֭בֶד (oshb:Prov.30.10, "do not slander a servant") to his אדנו/אֲדֹנָ֑יו (ketiv/qere pair, the unpointed form sitting inline before the pointed form at oshb:Prov.30.10), shares no anaphoric opening or catchword with the fourfold "generation" run that begins immediately after at web:Prov.30.11, so it stands as its own verse between the petuchah at oshb:Prov.30.9 (single-witness, disclosed) and that run.
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Grouping this verse with the four "generation" sayings that follow was considered because both concern household or family disorder, but 30:10 opens with a prohibition rather than the repeated "generation" noun that binds 30:11-14 together, so it is kept separate.
observed_substrate_signals: prohibition opener אַל תַּלְשֵׁ֣ן at oshb:Prov.30.10 (ketiv/qere verse; the K/Q pair itself is the next signal)
ketiv אדנו before qere אֲדֹנָ֑יו at oshb:Prov.30.10
petuchah at the immediately preceding verse, oshb:Prov.30.9 (single-witness)
prev_row.device_notes: The inline unpointed-before-pointed ketiv/qere pattern at oshb:Prov.30.10 matches the book-wide kq layer's usual shape (69 notes total, sweep: 69) -- texture, not a boundary driver. This single_proverb is the byte-grounded deviation from C6's numerical-saying default: the verse opens without a numeral and links to neither neighbor by anaphora.

next_row.boundary_rationale: The leech's two daughters, שְׁתֵּ֥י בָנוֹת֮ (oshb:Prov.30.15, "two daughters"), pivot straight into the chapter's first explicit three/four formula, שָׁל֣וֹשׁ ... אַ֝רְבַּ֗ע (oshb:Prov.30.15, "three ... four"), whose four unsatisfied appetites -- Sheol, the barren womb, the earth, and fire -- are named in 30:16 alone (4 of 4 there, oshb:Prov.30.16). The petuchah at oshb:Prov.30.14 (single-witness, disclosed) opens the unit, and the layer records a mark at neither of its own two verses, so the numeral and its own list are kept together as one function unit.
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating 30:15 and 30:16 as separate rows -- the leech image alone, then the four-item list alone -- was considered, but the four-thing tally opened in 30:15 (4 of 4) is not settled until 30:16 supplies its members, so splitting there would cut the numeral from its own list.
